topic: Bretton Woods Twins: IMF and World Bank (Economics)
description: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 resulted in the creation of two major international financial institutions: the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. Known as the 'Bretton Woods Twins', they were established to rebuild the post-WWII global economy, ensure financial stability, and promote development.

sections.title: Historical Background
sections.description: The origins and foundational events that led to the establishment of the global financial architecture.

historical_events.significance: Officially known as the United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference, delegates from 44 Allied nations met in New Hampshire, USA, to sign the agreements establishing the IMF and the IBRD (World Bank).
Both institutions officially came into existence in December 1945 and later set up their headquarters in Washington D.C., USA.

key_associations.item: John Maynard Keynes and Harry Dexter White
key_associations.associated_with: Founding Fathers of the Bretton Woods System
key_associations.extra_info: They were the principal architects who drafted the framework for the post-war international monetary system.

sections.title: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
sections.description: The IMF focuses on fostering global monetary cooperation, securing financial stability, and facilitating international trade.

key_concepts.explanation: The IMF primarily provides short-term loans and financial assistance to member countries struggling with Balance of Payments (BoP) crises to help them stabilize their economies.
Created by the IMF in 1969, it is an international reserve asset also known as 'Paper Gold'. It is used to supplement the official reserves of its member countries.
Every member country is assigned a quota based on its relative economic position in the world economy. This quota determines its maximum financial commitment to the IMF and its voting power.

important_facts.fact: The value of the SDR is based on a basket of five major international currencies: US Dollar, Euro, Chinese Renminbi (Yuan), Japanese Yen, and British Pound Sterling.

sections.title: World Bank Group (WBG)
sections.description: The World Bank Group provides long-term loans, grants, and technical assistance for capital projects in developing nations. It consists of 5 distinct institutions.

key_concepts.concept: IBRD (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
key_concepts.explanation: It provides loans and financial assistance to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries. Historically, IBRD is the institution originally referred to as the 'World Bank'.
It provides zero-to-low-interest loans (credits) and grants to the poorest developing countries. It is famously known as the 'Soft Loan Window' of the World Bank.
It focuses exclusively on the private sector, providing investment, advisory, and asset-management services to encourage private enterprise in developing countries.

important_facts.fact: The other two institutions of the WBG are the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID).
India is a founding member of IBRD, IDA, IFC, and MIGA, but India is NOT a member of ICSID.

sections.title: Major Publications and Reports
sections.description: Crucial annual analytical reports published by the Bretton Woods institutions that track global economic health.

key_associations.extra_info: It provides a comprehensive analysis of global economic developments, growth projections, and future prospects, usually published twice a year.
It assesses the key risks facing the global financial system and international capital markets.
An invaluable analytical report published annually, with each edition focusing on a specific, critical development theme (e.g., poverty, agriculture, education).

sections.title: India and the Bretton Woods Twins
sections.description: India's historical engagement and structural facts regarding the IMF and the World Bank.

historical_events.significance: India faced a severe Balance of Payments crisis and approached the IMF for an emergency bailout. As a condition for the loan, India had to introduce sweeping LPG (Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization) structural reforms.

important_facts.fact: India is a founding member of both the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank.
By an unwritten convention, the President of the World Bank is historically an American citizen nominated by the US, while the Managing Director of the IMF is a European.
